messages:
ashok: Heads-up — I tried a narrower micro-batch interval (8ms -> 4ms) + added 1.5ms coalesce jitter on the staging pool this morning. Seeing a weird regression in p95 token latency and a kernel selection change in the profiler :thinking_face:

sophie: Interesting. What do you mean by kernel selection change? Any logs from the runtime? :eyes:

ashok: Perf traces show that when we tighten the window, the runtime starts picking the 'fallback_attn_v2' kernel for many requests instead of 'fast_attn_qk_opt'. Seems correlated with increased average sequence length inside a microbatch. I pasted the snippet from the profiler below:

```
# sample from kernel_selector.log
batch_id=3589 seq_len_mean=412 seq_len_max=1024 pick=fast_attn_qk_opt
batch_id=3611 seq_len_mean=518 seq_len_max=1024 pick=fallback_attn_v2
```

tim: Huh. So reducing delay reduced batching across short-prefix traffic, but it increased coalescing of long tails? That could push mean seq_len over the threshold your selector uses. Did you change the selection cutoff recently?

ashok: No selector cutoff changes. The selector uses heuristics: if seq_len_mean > 480 or max > 768 we prefer fallback for correctness/oom safety. With smaller interval we ended up with more heterogeneous microbatches — short requests joined with sessions that have warmed KV and reach >768.

natalie: Could KV cache priming be causing inflated seq lengths? If requests pick up cached KV, they pass through longer decoder steps? Or do you mean requests actually request more tokens?

ashok: It's not extra user tokens. It's internal tokenization divergence + a small bug in prefix-trim that left leading padding for some streams; those count toward seq_len in the selector. Fixing that reduced mean seq_len by ~30 tokens. But p95 still up ~8% vs baseline.

perf-bot: CI perf-check: continuous-batching microbench vs baseline -> p50 +2%, p95 +8.1%, token-cost -1.2% (due to better batching). See https://ci.internal/reports/1912345678

tim: +8% p95 is pretty bad. Can we try increasing jitter magnitude instead of reducing interval? My hypothesis: jitter helps avoid pathological sync across long sequences, while keeping interval higher avoids merging too many long sessions into the same microbatch.

ashok: I ran a quick A/B: (4ms interval, 1.5ms jitter) vs (8ms interval, 6ms jitter). Results: the 8/6 configuration brought p95 back to baseline and reduced kernel fallback rate by ~70%. However median latency increased 3ms.

sophie: Tradeoff looks acceptable if p95 stays bounded. Do we have token budget violations or queue growth under 8/6?

ashok: Queue length was slightly higher under burst peaks (median queue depth +0.6 requests per worker) but no SLA violations in the 1h soak. Token budget target adherence was unchanged — we still hit the per-request token budget cap.

natalie: Can we instrument a tiny feature: log "selector_input_stats" per microbatch to trace seq_len distribution, kv_hit_rate, and first_request_age? That might let us tweak a smarter policy (e.g., if kv_hit_rate high && seq_len_variance high -> bias toward smaller coalesce).

tim: +1 for selector_input_stats. Also, I want an experiment that keeps interval low but biases joining to similar seq_len buckets. E.g., when a request arrives, look at head-of-queue seq_len_mean and only join if within +/- 40 tokens, else wait up to jitter_max. Might keep median low and avoid kernel churn.

ashok: I'll prototype bucketed-join. Quick pseudocode:
```
if abs(incoming.seq_len - head.seq_len_mean) <= BUCKET_DELTA:
  join
else:
  wait up to jitter_max
```
Will run a 2hr job on staging.

sophie: Also add an alert if we flip kernels > 20% of batches in 10min. That would catch regressions early.

perf-bot: perf-alert: kernel-flip rate currently 12% across staging pool. Config trial 8/6 -> 3%.

natalie: FYI, I found one more source of noise: client-side streaming SDK sometimes sends an empty "continue" token which increments seq_len count in the runtime. We're adding server-side dedupe for that event. Should remove ~5-10 tokens per request on average.

ashok: Plan for next steps: 1) commit fix for prefix-trim + client dedupe (rollout today) 2) add selector_input_stats logging + alert 3) prototype bucketed-join 4) run 24h soak of 8ms interval + 6ms jitter vs 4ms+1.5ms on staging and collect kernel selection + p95.

sophie: Sounds good. Can you post the experiment config in the repo and tag me? I'll help analyze traces. :thumbsup:

ashok: Yep — will push config and thread updates after the fix. Thanks all :)
